American store clothing size is numbered smaller than American custom, tailored, formal dress size. Europe, UK, Italy, and France also have their own size charts. A person's body is going to measure the same on a measuring tape no matter what country they're in, though, so it's just a matter of measuring, converting to metric, and being either a size 0, size 12, size 44, size 36, etc.

Italy's clothing seems to be numbered almost the same between tailored and non. Most of my clothes are bought in stores and are a 42 (US size 6) with the odd 40 (US size 4) thrown in. The few tailored items I have are also in a 42, and my wedding dress (yay!) is a 40.

Store sizes and "formal dress" sizes are different in America. You can be a size 2 in most stores, but if you go to get a high-end wedding dress custom tailored, it will technically be a "size 12" or so, like in the chart that I linked above.

Burda is a European company and does have its own European sizes in cm measurements. Here is a comparison. UK, Italy, and France also have their own size charts.
